hints: Notice the cylinder displaces a volume set by its own size $A$ and $X$, while $H$ only tells you how far the top face is below the surface of liquid.
Recall that upthrust equals the weight of displaced fluid, so it must involve the liquid density $\rho_L$ and not the cylinder density $\rho_C$.
Write displaced mass as $\rho_L$ times displaced volume $AX$, then multiply by $g$ to get the upthrust force and check which expression matches.
walkthrough: Find the volume of liquid displaced by the fully submerged cylinder. From the diagram, volume $= $ cross-sectional area times length $= AX$.
State the governing rule: Archimedes principle says upthrust $= $ weight of displaced liquid $= $ mass of displaced liquid times $g$.
Find the displaced mass using $m = \rho V$ for the liquid: $m = \rho_L A X$.
Multiply by $g$ to get weight: upthrust $= \rho_L A X g$. The depth $H$ affects the pressure on both faces equally in the difference, so it does not appear in the final upthrust.
This matches $\rho_L A X g$. This is option D.

options.A: This uses cylinder density $\rho_C$ and depth $H$, which gives neither the weight of the cylinder nor the weight of displaced liquid.
options.B: This is $\rho_C A X g$, which is the weight of the solid cylinder, not the upthrust from the displaced liquid.
options.C: This uses liquid density $\rho_L$ but volume $AH$, which is the liquid column above the cylinder, not the volume displaced by the cylinder.
options.D: This is the weight of displaced liquid $\rho_L$ times cylinder volume $AX$ times $g$, which equals the upthrust by Archimedes principle.
